Subject: POC trial environment setup - hosted vs dedicated vs VPC (next steps)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today — really appreciate the context on your evaluation goals. Per our conversation, I wanted to summarize the recommended next steps and the key decisions we need from your side to get the POC scheduled.

Quick recap / success criteria (please confirm or edit):
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 300ms for chat flow with 1k token window
- Throughput: support ~50 concurrent agents with acceptable tail latency
- Cost: cost-per-1k-tokens target for evaluation (we can provide estimates)
- Quality: match or exceed current baseline for intent classification (per your eval set)
- Security: no customer PII leaves your VPC for the final validation

Environment options we discussed (tradeoffs):
1) Hosted sandbox (fastest onboarding) — Redwood-managed, quickest to iterate, lower up-front ops; good for early functional checks and prompt tuning.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity) — predictable throughput, isolated compute; better for load testing and performance parity with production-like hardware.
3) VPC trial (private deployment) — customer VPC or peered VPC, required for final security validation; longest lead time (network + security reviews).

Suggested approach (recommended):
- Phase 1 (1 week): Hosted sandbox to validate quality and run initial eval set.
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): Dedicated sandbox for throughput/load checks and tuning.
- Phase 3 (2+ weeks): VPC trial for security validation and sign-off (if required).

Action items / asks from Acme AI:
- Confirm success criteria above (who will own metric sign-off?).
- Confirm target timeline (are you ok with the phased approach above?).
- Provide a technical contact for VPC onboarding (AWS account ID, security POC).
- Let us know procurement/contract constraints — procurement contact cc'd if needed.

Attachments: Redwood_POC_Checklist.pdf, Hosted_vs_Dedicated_vs_VPC_one-pager.pdf

Proposed next steps:
- If you confirm hosted sandbox as Phase 1, I can spin up access and schedule a 30-min kickoff with you and Priya for Wed 3/4 or Thu 3/5.
- Rishi will follow up on pricing options for dedicated capacity and VPC license implications.

Thanks —

Quick pricing guidance to help procurement: these are ballpark estimates for the evaluation phases (we'll produce a formal quote once the scope is locked):
- Hosted sandbox: $0 (trial credits) up to ~$2k for heavy usage beyond free tier (recommended initial phase).
- Dedicated sandbox (reserved short-term): ~$4k-$8k/week depending on GPU type and concurrency needs.
- VPC trial (private deployment): one-time onboarding/setup fee (~$6k) + ongoing reserved capacity pricing; operational overhead for network/security reviews may add time/cost.

Recommendation: start hosted sandbox (zero friction) -> move to dedicated for load testing -> parallelize VPC security review now so it can be greenlighted while we run functional tests.

PII / VPC onboarding notes from engineering:
- For a VPC trial we need:
  - AWS account ID(s) and the CIDR ranges to allowlist
  - IAM service account or role that we can use for limited access (we provide a template)
  - If you prefer peering, please confirm VPC ID and region and whether cross-account peering is allowed
  - Expected number of concurrent connections and average payload sizes (helps sizing)
- Typical lead time for VPC trial (security + network approvals): 7-14 business days after we receive the above items and the filled questionnaire.

If you want to accelerate, we can do the hosted sandbox first (no network work) and I can start a parallel thread with your infra team to gather the VPC items.
